To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified candidate proteins that may be involved in the pathogenesis of Fragile X and autism spectrum disorders.

the lipid raft proteomes of Fmr1 KO and WT mice are significantly different, and that the differentially represented proteins in the Fmr1 KO raft are involved in the regulation of myelin and axonal processes, and that these differentially represented proteins are connected by functional interactions.

In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common form of inherited intellectual disability, arises from transcriptionally silencing of the gene encoding an RNA binding protein (Fragile X Mental Retaration Protein or FMRP) and how it leads to the pleiotropic effects observed in FXS patients.
understanding how FMRP deficiency leads to changes in the lipid raft proteomes and how this may contribute to autism and intellectual disability in Fragile X syndrome.

the study of molecular mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of Fragile X mental retardation syndrome, an autism spectrum disorder caused by the silencing of a specific gene, FMR1, encoding an RNA-binding and translational regulator, Fragile X mental Retardation Protein, or FMRP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results suggest that FMRP is required to maintain the integrity of lipid raft proteome in neurons and that lipid rafts may play a role in Fragile X syndrome pathophysiology.
our results indicate that the absence of Fmr1 in mice leads to a dysregulation of the lipid raft proteomic profile.
the Fmr1 KO mouse brain has a lipid raft proteome which is distinct from that of the WT brain, and this difference may be a contributing factor in the pathophysiology of FXS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FMRP protein is a critical regulator of the lipid raft proteomic profile in the brain, and that this regulation is disrupted in the Fragile X syndrome mouse model.
FMRP regulates lipid raft proteome, and that the lipid raft proteomic profile of Fmr1 KO mice is altered.
we have developed a quantitative mass spectrometer based approach to profile lipid rafts proteome in a mouse model of Fragile-X syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of Fmr1 results in changes in lipid raft proteome that are consistent with dysregulated lipid homeostasis, which could affect neuronal function and synaptic transmission.

the FMRP protein regulates the expression of proteins that participate in the formation of lipid rafts, which are specialized regions of cell membranes that are involved in the regulation of intracellular signalling.
Fmr1 silences a large number of genes encoding proteins involved in lipid metabolism and homeostasis.
